subject: Program Pulse: runway, risks, and QBR prep
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: platform@acmehealth.com, tara@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Program Pulse: runway, risks, and QBR prep

Team — quick weekly pulse ahead of QBR prep window. TL;DR: momentum on latency SLO, two operational risks to surface, three asks for next 48 hours. Attached: updated QBR deck v2.

Wins
- Latency team landed the KV-cache optimizer (v1) behind feature flag; observed 18% p95 token latency improvement in staging on long-context workloads. Big win for Hosted API performance story.
- Acme Health pilot: initial feedback positive — integration tests complete and first sandbox traffic flowing.
- Billing infra: finalized per-route cost breakdowns for Dedicated customers; will help pricing discussion.

Risks / Open Issues
1) Dedicated capacity autoscaler: under certain burst patterns the scheduler misses scale-up window — observed in stress tests with long-running batched jobs. Mitigation work is in flight but ETA is 72 hrs. Impact: potential latency degradation for reserved tenants during end-of-quarter load.
2) QBR narrative gap: we need a crisp example that ties our cost controls (batching + KV cache) to a measurable unit-economics improvement for a representative customer. Acme Health is a good candidate but we need the cost delta computed.

Asks (concrete, please)
- @jonas_weber: can you validate autoscaler mitigation plan and confirm whether the 72-hr ETA is still realistic? If not, propose a rollback/fallback policy for Dean/Legal to sign off.
- @laura_bennett: please draft a 1-slide cost delta case using Acme pilot numbers (even provisional). I can help align with Acme.
- @vanessa_ortiz + @kimberly_park: please coordinate a 30-min sync with Acme platform (cc'd) this week to capture usage patterns we can model for the slide.

Logistics / QBR timeline
- I want a final slide deck by EOD Oct 12 to circulate to execs for review on Oct 13. Suggest we keep the QBR narrative: 1) reliability wins, 2) cost-econ example, 3) roadmap ask (autoscaler hardening + fallback), 4) customer testimonial (Acme).

Attachments: QBR_prep_slide_deck_v2.pptx

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com


From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Program Pulse: runway, risks, and QBR prep

Sergio — thanks for the summary, good framing. Quick notes:
- I can run the Acme cost-delta slide but need the rough numbers by EOD Oct 11 (traffic, avg seq length, tokens saved by cache). If Acme can't share exact numbers, a modeled example with conservative assumptions will work.
- On autoscaler: if the 72-hr fix is tight, let's outline a short-term SLA credit or capacity buffer we can offer to affected Dedicated customers. Legal will need the language; happy to draft.

I'll aim to circulate a first draft slide by Oct 12 AM.

Laura Bennett
Chief of Staff to CEO | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Program Pulse: runway, risks, and QBR prep

Sergio / team — status on autoscaler: root cause identified (race between burst evaluation and node provisioning when batched jobs hold GPUs warm). Mitigation plan: 1) short-term: reduce evaluation window and add conservative overprovisioning threshold; 2) medium: fast-path provisioning hook for preemptive warm nodes. Short-term patch is ready, but needs a Canary roll tomorrow; if Canary is green, we can push to prod by Oct 13. That aligns with the 72-hr window if we start the Canary Monday morning.

I've attached a compact pipeline snapshot illustrating recent burst patterns that triggered the issue. Use it for the QBR slide/modeling.

Attachments: pipeline_snapshot_oct2026.xlsx

On the customer-side, Acme platform team shared some sample request traces (low-volume). They permissioned a slightly broader access for modeling — Vanessa, can you take point on the sync?

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@acmehealth.com>, platform@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Program Pulse: runway, risks, and QBR prep

Appreciate the quick responses and the patch plan, Jonas — good work. Short recap and next steps (action tracker):

1) Autoscaler (Jonas) — start Canary Mon AM (Oct 12). If green, push to Prod Oct 13. Please post progress in #prod-autoscaler and ping me if Canary metrics don't meet thresholds.
2) Acme cost slide (Laura + Sergio) — Laura will draft slide; I'll follow up with Acme to gather the missing traffic and seq-length notes today. Vanessa to run the 30-min sync and capture traces.
3) Exec deck — I'll fold the autoscaler mitigation summary and the modeled Acme delta into the final deck and circulate by EOD Oct 12 for exec review.

Customer ask: Tara — thanks for the traces you shared. If possible, could you confirm we can use anonymized sample traces in a public-facing case study? If not, we'll keep the slide strictly internal to execs.

I will also draft a fallback sentence for Legal re: temporary capacity buffer in case the Canary does not stabilize traffic quickly. Laura — if you could draft the customer-facing credit language, that would be helpful.

Closing note: good momentum (latency win + Acme onboarding) — keeping focus on the autoscaler is the right call.

Thanks all — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
